title: Discovering the Côte de Beaune
description: An in-depth tour of Burgundy's white wine paradise — explore Meursault, Puligny-Montrachet, Chassagne-Montrachet and the ultimate expression of Chardonnay.
lessons.0.title: Côte de Beaune Overview: A White Wine Paradise
lessons.0.slides.0.title: Côte de Beaune Overview: A White Wine Paradise
lessons.0.slides.0.subtitle: 12 minutes
lessons.0.slides.0.description: The Côte de Beaune is the southern half of the Côte d'Or, world-renowned for its top-tier Chardonnay whites. Reds are also produced, but the whites carry the greater fame — Meursault, Puligny-Montrachet and Chassagne-Montrachet are pilgrimage sites for any white-wine lover.
lessons.0.slides.1.title: 🗺️ Map of the Côte de Beaune
lessons.0.slides.2.title: Geography and Climate
lessons.0.slides.2.content: The Côte de Beaune stretches roughly 25 km from Ladoix down to Maranges. Compared with the Côte de Nuits, the topography is more complex, slopes face in many directions, and soils are more varied — creating room for both great reds and great whites.
lessons.0.slides.2.keyPoints.0: Climate: slightly warmer than the Côte de Nuits, well suited to Chardonnay
lessons.0.slides.2.keyPoints.1: Soils: limestone-based, with a higher proportion of marl
lessons.0.slides.2.keyPoints.2: Topography: valleys and slopes interweave; significant micro-climatic variation
lessons.0.slides.3.title: What Makes the Côte de Beaune Unique
lessons.0.slides.3.content: The Côte de Beaune is the heart of Burgundy white wine. It is home to six white-wine Grands Crus — the most expensive Chardonnay terroirs on earth — while still producing outstanding Pinot Noir. Eighteen village-level AOCs deliver remarkable diversity.
lessons.0.slides.3.keyPoints.0: 🏆 White Grands Crus: six of the world's most expensive Chardonnay sites (all clustered around Montrachet)
lessons.0.slides.3.keyPoints.1: 🍷 Red wine villages: Pommard and Volnay are stylistically very different yet equally fine
lessons.0.slides.3.keyPoints.2: 💎 Best value: village-level Beaune offers exceptional bang for the buck
lessons.0.slides.3.keyPoints.3: 🎨 Stylistic range: from mineral to buttery, from powerful to elegant
lessons.0.slides.3.keyPoints.4: 📊 Production split: 60% white, 40% red (the inverse of the Côte de Nuits)
lessons.0.slides.3.keyPoints.5: 🌟 Eighteen village AOCs — the most diverse stretch in Burgundy
lessons.0.slides.4.title: 💡 Key Take-aways
lessons.0.slides.4.points.0: 🍾 60% of the Côte de Beaune is white — Chardonnay is the lead
lessons.0.slides.4.points.1: 🍾 The white Grands Crus all cluster around Montrachet
lessons.0.slides.4.points.2: 🍾 The reds are less famous than those of the Côte de Nuits but every bit as fine
lessons.0.slides.5.title: 🧠 Knowledge Check
lessons.0.slides.5.questions.0.question: What style of wine is the Côte de Beaune most famous for?
lessons.0.slides.5.questions.0.explanati: The Côte de Beaune is the heartland of the world's greatest white wines. Chardonnay from Meursault, Puligny-Montrachet and Chassagne-Montrachet is regarded as a global benchmark. There are also fine Pinot Noir reds such as Pommard and Volnay.
lessons.0.slides.5.questions.1.question: What is "Le Montrachet"?
lessons.0.slides.5.questions.1.options.0: A. Burgundy's most famous Pinot Noir Grand Cru
lessons.0.slides.5.questions.1.options.1: B. The Grand Cru widely regarded as the world's greatest white wine (Chardonnay)
lessons.0.slides.5.questions.1.options.2: C. One of the ten Cru villages of Beaujolais
lessons.0.slides.5.questions.1.explanati: "Le Montrachet" (usually just Montrachet) is a 7-hectare white-wine Grand Cru straddling Puligny-Montrachet and Chassagne-Montrachet. Its minerality and complexity make it widely regarded as the greatest dry Chardonnay in the world.
lessons.0.slides.5.questions.2.question: Which of the following are famous Chardonnay villages of the Côte de Beaune? (multiple answers)
lessons.0.slides.5.questions.2.explanati: Meursault, Puligny-Montrachet and Chassagne-Montrachet are the "three great white-wine villages" of the Côte de Beaune, each producing a distinct Chardonnay style — Meursault for its buttery weight, Puligny for mineral elegance, Chassagne for full-bodied complexity. Gevrey-Chambertin lies in the Côte de Nuits and is famous for red wine.
lessons.0.slides.5.questions.3.question: Pommard and Volnay are the standard-bearers for what style on the Côte de Beaune?
lessons.0.slides.5.questions.3.options.1: B. Outstanding Pinot Noir red-wine villages
lessons.0.slides.5.questions.3.options.3: D. Mineral whites in the Chablis style
lessons.0.slides.5.questions.3.explanati: Pommard (deeply coloured, powerful, requires age) and Volnay (elegant and lithe, floral, drinkable young) are the two most famous Pinot Noir villages of the Côte de Beaune. Neither has a Grand Cru, but both boast many outstanding Premiers Crus.
lessons.0.slides.5.questions.4.question: What is the most famous annual wine event in the town of Beaune?
lessons.0.slides.5.questions.4.options.1: B. The Hospices de Beaune Auction
lessons.0.slides.5.questions.4.options.2: C. The Côte d'Or Wine Fair
lessons.0.slides.5.questions.4.explanati: Held on the third weekend of November, the Hospices de Beaune Auction is the world's oldest charity wine auction. It has run since 1859, with proceeds funding the hospital, and serves as a key barometer for Burgundy vintage prices.
lessons.0.slides.6.title: Summary
lessons.0.slides.6.content: The Côte de Beaune showcases Chardonnay at its very best — from the buttery weight of Meursault to the steely minerality of Puligny — every village with its own unmistakable charm.
lessons.1.title: The Three White-Wine Villages: Meursault, Puligny, Chassagne
lessons.1.slides.0.title: The Three White-Wine Villages: Meursault, Puligny, Chassagne
lessons.1.slides.0.subtitle: 18 minutes
lessons.1.slides.0.description: The three great white-wine villages of the Côte de Beaune embody three faces of Chardonnay: the buttery, hazelnut-laced Meursault; the mineral, refined Puligny; and Chassagne, where reds and whites stand side by side.
lessons.1.slides.1.title: 🗺️ Map of the Three White-Wine Villages
lessons.1.slides.1.regions.0.name: Meursault
lessons.1.slides.1.regions.0.description: The classic for butter and hazelnut
lessons.1.slides.1.regions.1.name: Puligny-Montrachet
lessons.1.slides.1.regions.2.name: Chassagne-Montrachet
lessons.1.slides.1.regions.2.description: Both red and white, three Grands Crus
lessons.1.slides.2.title: The "White Wine Golden Triangle" — A Stylistic Spectrum
lessons.1.slides.2.caption: Three extreme expressions of Chardonnay across three top villages: purity, roundness and power
lessons.1.slides.3.title: Meursault: The Classic for Butter and Hazelnut
lessons.1.slides.3.content: Meursault is the largest white-wine village of the Côte de Beaune. Although it has no Grand Cru, the Premier Cru wines are of the highest quality. Its hallmark aromas are butter, hazelnut and toasted bread.
lessons.1.slides.3.keyPoints.0: Area: 395 ha (the largest white-wine village of the Côte de Beaune)
lessons.1.slides.3.keyPoints.1: Premiers Crus: 13 sites of exceptional quality
lessons.1.slides.3.keyPoints.2: Style: butter, hazelnut, toasted bread; round and full
lessons.1.slides.4.title: Top Premiers Crus of Meursault
lessons.1.slides.4.content: There is no Grand Cru, but these Premier Cru sites can rival Grand Cru quality.
lessons.1.slides.4.keyPoints.0: 🍾 Perrières — closest to Grand Cru level, with a strong mineral lift
lessons.1.slides.4.keyPoints.3: 🍾 Poruzots — power and elegance hand in hand
lessons.1.slides.5.title: Puligny-Montrachet: Mineral Elegance
lessons.1.slides.5.content: Puligny-Montrachet is home to four Grands Crus and produces some of the world's most refined Chardonnay — intensely mineral, vibrantly acidic, with extraordinary ageing potential.
lessons.1.slides.5.keyPoints.0: Four Grands Crus (the world's most expensive Chardonnay terroirs)
lessons.1.slides.5.keyPoints.1: Style: pronounced minerality, lively acidity, fine and elegant
lessons.1.slides.6.title: Grands Crus of Puligny-Montrachet (1/2)
lessons.1.slides.6.content: Montrachet is the king of white wines; together with Chevalier-Montrachet it represents the highest achievement of Chardonnay. Their position and terroir give each its singular personality.
lessons.1.slides.6.keyPoints.2: Position: mid-slope, perfect drainage, optimal sun exposure
lessons.1.slides.6.keyPoints.3: Price: €500–2,000 per bottle (top vintages can reach €5,000+)
lessons.1.slides.6.keyPoints.5: Style: ultimate complexity, profound elegance, perfect balance of power and finesse
lessons.1.slides.6.keyPoints.6: Aromas: white flowers, hazelnut, honey, mineral, toasted almond, butter
lessons.1.slides.6.keyPoints.7: Palate: creamy texture, endless finish, astonishing layers
lessons.1.slides.6.keyPoints.11: Position: above Montrachet — higher altitude, thinner topsoil
lessons.1.slides.6.keyPoints.14: Style: pronounced minerality, lively acidity, fine and refined, more reserved
lessons.1.slides.6.keyPoints.15: Character: lighter than Montrachet, but no less refined
lessons.1.slides.7.title: Grands Crus of Puligny-Montrachet (2/2)
lessons.1.slides.7.content: The two Grands Crus of the Bâtard family. They do not reach the very top of Montrachet, but remain world-class Chardonnay terroirs, each with its own profile.
lessons.1.slides.7.keyPoints.2: Position: below Montrachet — deeper soils with more clay
lessons.1.slides.7.keyPoints.5: Style: more powerful and full-bodied than Montrachet, more opulent
lessons.1.slides.7.keyPoints.6: Character: richer fruit, denser body — pairs with bolder dishes
lessons.1.slides.7.keyPoints.7: Aromas: ripe fruit, honey, butter, toasted hazelnut
lessons.1.slides.7.keyPoints.14: Style: elegant and refined, sitting between Bâtard and Chevalier
lessons.1.slides.7.keyPoints.15: Character: one of the smallest Grands Crus — tiny production but relatively good value
lessons.1.slides.8.title: Chassagne-Montrachet: Both Red and White
lessons.1.slides.8.content: Chassagne-Montrachet produces both red and white wine. The whites are mineral and elegant; the reds are also of high quality. The village shares three Grands Crus.
lessons.1.slides.8.keyPoints.0: Three Grands Crus (whole or partly in Chassagne)
lessons.1.slides.8.keyPoints.1: Whites: mineral, elegant, rounder than Puligny
lessons.1.slides.8.keyPoints.2: Reds: fine tannins, pure fruit, ageworthy
lessons.1.slides.9.title: Grands Crus of Chassagne-Montrachet
lessons.1.slides.9.content: Chassagne owns or shares three Grands Crus. Criots-Bâtard-Montrachet lies entirely within Chassagne. These sites express the village's rounder, fuller style.
lessons.1.slides.9.keyPoints.1: Area: about 4 ha within Chassagne (out of a total 7.5 ha)
lessons.1.slides.9.keyPoints.2: Position: the Chassagne side is generally a touch warmer
lessons.1.slides.9.keyPoints.3: Style: the king of white wines; the Chassagne portion is fuller and rounder
lessons.1.slides.9.keyPoints.7: Area: about 5.8 ha within Chassagne (out of a total 11.9 ha)
lessons.1.slides.9.keyPoints.8: Position: Chassagne holds the larger share
lessons.1.slides.9.keyPoints.9: Style: opulent and full; the Chassagne portion is denser
lessons.1.slides.9.keyPoints.14: Position: south of Bâtard, close to the centre of Chassagne village
lessons.1.slides.9.keyPoints.17: Style: one of the smallest Grands Crus — elegant and refined, but rounder than Puligny
lessons.1.slides.9.keyPoints.18: Character: tiny production, very rare, yet relatively accessible in price
lessons.1.slides.10.title: 💡 Key Take-aways
lessons.1.slides.10.points.0: 🍾 Meursault has no Grand Cru, but its top Premier Cru wines can rival Grand Cru quality
lessons.1.slides.10.points.1: 🍾 Montrachet is the world's most expensive Chardonnay, averaging well over €500
lessons.1.slides.10.points.2: 🍾 The reds of Chassagne are often underrated and offer excellent value

lessons.1.slides.11.questions.2.question: Which of the following are famous Chardonnay villages of the Côte de Beaune? (multiple answers)
lessons.1.slides.11.questions.2.explanat: Meursault, Puligny-Montrachet and Chassagne-Montrachet are the "three great white-wine villages" of the Côte de Beaune, each producing a distinct Chardonnay style — Meursault for its buttery weight, Puligny for mineral elegance, Chassagne for full-bodied complexity. Gevrey-Chambertin lies in the Côte de Nuits and is famous for red wine.

lessons.1.slides.12.title: Summary
lessons.1.slides.12.content: The three great white-wine villages capture the full range of Chardonnay — from butter to mineral — each with its own unmistakable charm.
lessons.2.title: The Red Wine Twins: Pommard and Volnay
lessons.2.slides.0.title: The Red Wine Twins: Pommard and Volnay
lessons.2.slides.0.subtitle: 12 minutes
lessons.2.slides.0.description: The two most famous red-wine villages of the Côte de Beaune. Pommard and Volnay sit side by side yet produce very different wines — a perfect illustration of how subtle terroir differences can be.
lessons.2.slides.1.title: 🗺️ Map of the Red Wine Twins
lessons.2.slides.1.regions.0.name: Pommard
lessons.2.slides.1.regions.0.description: The most powerful red, with 28 Premiers Crus
lessons.2.slides.1.regions.1.name: Volnay
lessons.2.slides.1.regions.1.description: The most elegant red, with 35 Premiers Crus
lessons.2.slides.2.title: Pommard: The Most Powerful Red of the Côte de Beaune
lessons.2.slides.2.content: Pommard makes only red wine. It is famed for thick tannins, firm structure and a need for long ageing. There is no Grand Cru, but the Premiers Crus are of the very highest quality.
lessons.2.slides.2.keyPoints.2: Style: thick tannins, firm structure, gamey aromatics
lessons.2.slides.3.title: Top Premiers Crus of Pommard
lessons.2.slides.3.content: There is no Grand Cru, but these Premier Cru sites are outstanding.
lessons.2.slides.3.keyPoints.0: 🍷 Les Rugiens — the finest Premier Cru of Pommard
lessons.2.slides.3.keyPoints.1: Powerful and concentrated, with stunning ageing potential
lessons.2.slides.3.keyPoints.7: The most elegant of the Pommard Premiers Crus
lessons.2.slides.4.title: Volnay: The Most Elegant Red of the Côte de Beaune
lessons.2.slides.4.content: Volnay also makes only red wine, but its style is the polar opposite of Pommard's — silky, refined and deeply floral, often described as the "feminine" Pinot Noir.
lessons.2.slides.4.keyPoints.2: Style: silky and refined, intensely floral, elegantly precise
lessons.2.slides.5.title: Top Premiers Crus of Volnay
lessons.2.slides.5.content: The pick of the 35 Premier Cru sites.
lessons.2.slides.5.keyPoints.0: 🍷 Caillerets — the most elegant and refined
lessons.2.slides.5.keyPoints.4: The most powerful of the Volnay Premiers Crus
lessons.2.slides.5.keyPoints.7: Yet the red wines may only be labelled Volnay (a unique quirk)
lessons.2.slides.6.title: Pommard vs Volnay: A Terroir Miracle
lessons.2.slides.6.content: Just 2 km apart, but two entirely different styles.
lessons.2.slides.6.keyPoints.0: 📍 Soils: Pommard high in clay vs Volnay limestone-driven
lessons.2.slides.6.keyPoints.1: 💪 Tannins: Pommard thick and powerful vs Volnay fine and supple
lessons.2.slides.6.keyPoints.2: 🌸 Aromatics: Pommard gamey black fruit vs Volnay violet and red fruit
lessons.2.slides.6.keyPoints.3: 🍷 Body: Pommard full and robust vs Volnay medium and refined
lessons.2.slides.6.keyPoints.4: ⏳ Ageing: Pommard 8–20 years vs Volnay 5–15 years
lessons.2.slides.6.keyPoints.5: 🎭 Style: Pommard masculine vs Volnay feminine
lessons.2.slides.7.title: 💡 Key Take-aways
lessons.2.slides.7.points.0: 🍷 Pommard and Volnay are only 2 km apart, yet stylistically worlds apart
lessons.2.slides.7.points.1: 🍷 Volnay's Santenots Premier Cru sits inside Meursault, but the wines may only be labelled Volnay
lessons.2.slides.7.points.2: 🍷 Neither village has a Grand Cru, but the Premier Cru level is exceptional

lessons.3.title: Other Key Villages and Tasting Recommendations
lessons.3.slides.0.title: Other Key Villages and Tasting Recommendations
lessons.3.slides.0.subtitle: 10 minutes
lessons.3.slides.0.description: Beyond the famous villages already covered, the Côte de Beaune holds many others worth exploring — they offer outstanding value and are perfect for newcomers.
lessons.3.slides.1.title: Aloxe-Corton: Red and White Grands Crus Side by Side
lessons.3.slides.1.content: The only village on the Côte de Beaune to hold both a red and a white Grand Cru — long-standing in history and exceptional in quality.
lessons.3.slides.1.keyPoints.1: 🍷 Reds: Corton is powerful and concentrated, with stunning ageing potential
lessons.3.slides.1.keyPoints.2: 🍾 Whites: Corton-Charlemagne is intensely mineral, elegant and complex
lessons.3.slides.1.keyPoints.3: 📍 Location: northern Côte de Beaune, on steep slopes
lessons.3.slides.1.keyPoints.5: ⭐ Notable: Charlemagne himself once owned vineyards here
lessons.3.slides.2.title: Beaune: Capital of the Côte de Beaune
lessons.3.slides.2.content: The largest village of the Côte de Beaune, with an astonishing 42 Premiers Crus — exceptional value and an ideal everyday option.
lessons.3.slides.2.keyPoints.0: 📊 Area: over 400 ha (the largest in the Côte de Beaune)
lessons.3.slides.2.keyPoints.2: 🍷 Style: predominantly red, elegant and easy-drinking, with pure fruit
lessons.3.slides.2.keyPoints.4: ⭐ Notable: the Hospices de Beaune charity auction
lessons.3.slides.2.keyPoints.5: 🎖️ Recommended: the king of value — perfect for beginners and everyday drinking

lessons.3.slides.3.description: Switch between History · Famous Cuvées · Auction Process to explore the 1443 origins, the naming logic of the 50 Cuvées, and the romantic candle-auction tradition.

lessons.3.slides.4.content: These villages offer consistent quality at accessible prices — a great gateway to the Côte de Beaune. The locations may not be as illustrious as the famous villages, but the terroir is excellent and many producers craft wines that punch well above their price point.

lessons.3.slides.5.title: Tasting Guidance: Beginner and Intermediate
lessons.3.slides.5.content: A step-by-step approach is the best way to learn about wine. Start with great-value villages, work up to the classic names, and build palate memory and tasting skills along the way.
lessons.3.slides.5.keyPoints.2: Goal: get to know the basic styles of Chardonnay and Pinot Noir
lessons.3.slides.5.keyPoints.3: Focus: butter vs mineral (white) and fruit vs tannin (red)
lessons.3.slides.5.keyPoints.5: Ageing: drink within 1–3 years of purchase
lessons.3.slides.5.keyPoints.6: Pairing: everyday home cooking, casual gatherings
lessons.3.slides.5.keyPoints.10: Recommended: Meursault Village, Volnay Village, Pommard Village
lessons.3.slides.5.keyPoints.11: Goal: understand differences in terroir and village character
lessons.3.slides.5.keyPoints.12: Focus: Meursault butter vs Puligny mineral
lessons.3.slides.5.keyPoints.14: Serving: open and decant reds 1–2 hours ahead
lessons.3.slides.5.keyPoints.17: Investment: a good fit for a small home cellar
lessons.3.slides.6.title: Tasting Guidance: Advanced and Collector
lessons.3.slides.6.content: Reaching the very top requires deep tasting experience and proper storage. These wines are not just for pleasure — they are works of art and serious investments.
lessons.3.slides.6.keyPoints.4: Goal: understand micro-climates, plot differences, and the impact of winemaking
lessons.3.slides.6.keyPoints.5: Focus: complexity, layering, finish length, ageing potential
lessons.3.slides.6.keyPoints.6: Serving: drink after 5–10 years, decant for 2–3 hours
lessons.3.slides.6.keyPoints.7: Storage: stable 12–14 °C, 70% humidity, dark, bottles laid flat
lessons.3.slides.6.keyPoints.8: Returns: 5–10% annual appreciation in strong vintages
lessons.3.slides.6.keyPoints.9: Best for: significant business occasions, collector tastings, investment portfolios
lessons.3.slides.6.keyPoints.14: Goal: experience Chardonnay at its absolute peak and grasp the essence of terroir
lessons.3.slides.6.keyPoints.15: Focus: ultimate complexity, endless finish, evolution with age
lessons.3.slides.6.keyPoints.16: Serving: 10–20 years for the peak window; decant for 3–4 hours
lessons.3.slides.6.keyPoints.17: Storage: professional cellar, stable temperature and humidity, long-term flat storage
lessons.3.slides.6.keyPoints.18: Investment: 10–20% annual appreciation in top vintages
lessons.3.slides.6.keyPoints.19: Buying tips: choose reputable merchants, verify provenance, watch the vintage
lessons.3.slides.6.keyPoints.20: Caveat: requires real tasting skill to be appreciated fully
lessons.3.slides.6.keyPoints.21: Best for: serious collectors, investment portfolios, life's milestone moments
lessons.3.slides.7.title: Food Pairing: Whites
lessons.3.slides.7.content: Côte de Beaune whites range from buttery and round to mineral and crisp. Different dishes bring out different facets — the key is balancing sauce and body.
lessons.3.slides.7.keyPoints.1: 🦞 Seafood: lobster, king crab, seafood in cream sauces
lessons.3.slides.7.keyPoints.2: 🍗 Poultry: roast chicken, turkey, chicken in cream sauce
lessons.3.slides.7.keyPoints.3: 🍄 Other: foie gras, creamed mushrooms, white-sauce pasta
lessons.3.slides.7.keyPoints.5: ⚠️ Avoid: very acidic dishes, sashimi, plain vegetables
lessons.3.slides.7.keyPoints.7: 💡 Pairing principle: the wine's creamy texture echoes the sauce
lessons.3.slides.7.keyPoints.10: 🦪 Seafood: oysters, scallops, sea urchin, steamed fish
lessons.3.slides.7.keyPoints.12: 🥗 Other: seafood salad, lemon-dressed fish, steamed shellfish
lessons.3.slides.7.keyPoints.13: 🧀 Cheese: goat cheese, fresh chèvre, feta
lessons.3.slides.7.keyPoints.16: 💡 Pairing principle: minerality marries seamlessly with seafood umami
lessons.3.slides.7.keyPoints.19: 🐟 Seafood: seared salmon, roast cod, seafood risotto
lessons.3.slides.7.keyPoints.20: 🍗 Poultry: roast chicken, chicken with mushrooms, coq au vin blanc
lessons.3.slides.7.keyPoints.21: 🍄 Other: creamed mushrooms, white truffle, lobster pasta
lessons.3.slides.7.keyPoints.24: 💡 Pairing principle: a midpoint between Meursault and Puligny
lessons.3.slides.8.title: Food Pairing: Reds
lessons.3.slides.8.content: Côte de Beaune Pinot Noir runs from powerful to elegant; common to all are fine tannins and pure fruit. When pairing, consider tannin strength and how mature the wine is.
lessons.3.slides.8.keyPoints.1: 🥩 Red meats: braised beef, steak, lamb chops, beef stew
lessons.3.slides.8.keyPoints.2: 🦆 Poultry: roast duck, goose, wild duck
lessons.3.slides.8.keyPoints.3: 🦌 Game: venison, wild boar, rabbit (rich preparations)
lessons.3.slides.8.keyPoints.4: 🧀 Cheese: aged Comté, Époisses, blue cheeses
lessons.3.slides.8.keyPoints.5: 🍄 Other: black truffle, wild-mushroom stews, beef bourguignon
lessons.3.slides.8.keyPoints.6: ⚠️ Avoid: light fish, raw preparations, simple dishes
lessons.3.slides.8.keyPoints.8: ⏰ Decanting: 2–3 hours for young wines, 1–2 hours for mature
lessons.3.slides.8.keyPoints.9: 💡 Pairing principle: powerful tannins need fat and protein to balance
lessons.3.slides.8.keyPoints.12: 🍗 Poultry: roast chicken, turkey, chicken with mushrooms, duck breast
lessons.3.slides.8.keyPoints.13: 🐰 Game: braised rabbit, hare, pheasant (lighter preparations)
lessons.3.slides.8.keyPoints.14: 🍄 Mushrooms: any mushroom dish, truffle, wild-mushroom risotto
lessons.3.slides.8.keyPoints.15: 🧀 Cheese: mild Brie, Camembert, young Comté
lessons.3.slides.8.keyPoints.16: 🥩 Other: veal, pork loin, salmon (rich preparations)
lessons.3.slides.8.keyPoints.17: ⚠️ Avoid: very heavy flavours, spicy, deep-fried
lessons.3.slides.8.keyPoints.20: 💡 Pairing principle: fine tannins suit medium-flavoured dishes
lessons.3.slides.8.keyPoints.23: 🍗 Poultry: roast chicken, roast duck legs, chicken dishes
lessons.3.slides.8.keyPoints.24: 🥩 Red meats: beef stew, beef burgers, roast pork chop
lessons.3.slides.8.keyPoints.25: 🍄 Other: mushroom dishes, red-wine stews, ragù pasta
lessons.3.slides.8.keyPoints.29: 💡 Pairing principle: approachable and versatile, a daily go-to
lessons.3.slides.9.title: 💡 Buying Tips
lessons.3.slides.9.points.0: 🍾 Beaune is the king of value, perfect for everyday drinking
lessons.3.slides.9.points.1: 🍾 Village-level Meursault is already very fine; the Premiers Crus are even better
lessons.3.slides.9.points.2: 🍾 White Grand Cru is expensive — Premier Cru is far better value
lessons.3.slides.9.points.3: 🍾 Saint-Romain and Auxey-Duresses are excellent entry points
lessons.3.slides.9.points.4: 🍾 Pommard needs at least 8 years' ageing; Volnay is enjoyable from 5
lessons.3.slides.9.points.5: 🍾 When buying, the producer matters more than the appellation
lessons.3.slides.10.title: 🧠 Knowledge Check
lessons.3.slides.10.questions.0.question: What style of wine is the Côte de Beaune most famous for?
lessons.3.slides.10.questions.0.explanat: The Côte de Beaune is the heartland of the world's greatest white wines. Chardonnay from Meursault, Puligny-Montrachet and Chassagne-Montrachet is regarded as a global benchmark. There are also fine Pinot Noir reds such as Pommard and Volnay.
lessons.3.slides.10.questions.1.question: What is "Le Montrachet"?
A. Burgundy's most famous Pinot Noir Grand Cru
B. The Grand Cru widely regarded as the world's greatest white wine (Chardonnay)
C. One of the ten Cru villages of Beaujolais
lessons.3.slides.10.questions.1.explanat: "Le Montrachet" (usually just Montrachet) is a 7-hectare white-wine Grand Cru straddling Puligny-Montrachet and Chassagne-Montrachet. Its minerality and complexity make it widely regarded as the greatest dry Chardonnay in the world.
lessons.3.slides.10.questions.2.question: Which of the following are famous Chardonnay villages of the Côte de Beaune? (multiple answers)
lessons.3.slides.10.questions.2.explanat: Meursault, Puligny-Montrachet and Chassagne-Montrachet are the "three great white-wine villages" of the Côte de Beaune, each producing a distinct Chardonnay style — Meursault for its buttery weight, Puligny for mineral elegance, Chassagne for full-bodied complexity. Gevrey-Chambertin lies in the Côte de Nuits and is famous for red wine.
lessons.3.slides.10.questions.3.question: Pommard and Volnay are the standard-bearers for what style on the Côte de Beaune?
B. Outstanding Pinot Noir red-wine villages
D. Mineral whites in the Chablis style
lessons.3.slides.10.questions.3.explanat: Pommard (deeply coloured, powerful, requires age) and Volnay (elegant and lithe, floral, drinkable young) are the two most famous Pinot Noir villages of the Côte de Beaune. Neither has a Grand Cru, but both boast many outstanding Premiers Crus.
lessons.3.slides.10.questions.4.question: What is the most famous annual wine event in the town of Beaune?
B. The Hospices de Beaune Auction
C. The Côte d'Or Wine Fair
lessons.3.slides.10.questions.4.explanat: Held on the third weekend of November, the Hospices de Beaune Auction is the world's oldest charity wine auction. It has run since 1859, with proceeds funding the hospital, and serves as a key barometer for Burgundy vintage prices.
lessons.3.slides.11.title: Summary
lessons.3.slides.11.content: Beyond the famous names, the Côte de Beaune is rich in great-value villages well worth exploring. Choose the level that suits your budget, pair the wines thoughtfully, build your tasting skills step by step — and enjoy the full diversity of Burgundy's reds and whites.
